subject: [PATCH v4 2/4] mm/huge_memory: don't queue folios when underused splitting is inactive

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that khugepaged/max_ptes_none is rarely changed during application runtime, and suggested this patch's assumption about its default value being the maximum is reasonable.
reviews.raw_body:
This sounds reasonable. In production, as far as I know from speaking with folks
in conferences, no one changes the value during application runtime
(atleast this is true in meta). Its usually only changed before the workload
starts (or just at boot time).

Acked-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>

2026-11-03.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's huge memory management to prevent anonymous PMD-sized folios from being queued for underused splitting when the system is configured to tolerate any number of zero-filled pages. This change is made by factoring out a check into a new function, thp_underused_never(), which is used in both deferred_split_folio() and thp_underused(). The patch also addresses an issue where folios that were already scanned are not requeued when the sysctl changes.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kiryl Shutsemau added a Reviewed-by tag to the patch, indicating they have reviewed it and are willing to vouch for its correctness.
